    • If nodes belong to different sets, union them and add cost
  • Continue until all villages connected

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

for i in \[0..N]:
make\_set(i)
edges = pipes + \[(wells\[i], 0, i+1) for i in range(N)]
sort edges by cost
total\_cost = 0
for cost, u, v in edges:
if find(u) != find(v):
union(u, v)
total\_cost += cost
return total\_cost

Code Implementation:

import java.util.*;

public class Main {

    // Parent array to store parent of each component of DSU.
    static int[] parent = new int[1001];

    // Size array to apply DSU by size.
    static int[] sizez = new int[1001];

    // This function is used to initialize the DSU.
    static void make(int i) {
        parent[i] = i;
        sizez[i] = 1;
    }

    // This function is used to find the parent of each component of DSU.
    static int find(int v) {
        if (v == parent[v])
            return v;
        return parent[v] = find(parent[v]);
    }

    // This function is used to merge two components of DSU.
    static void Union(int a, int b) {
        // Finding the parents of vertex a and b.
        a = find(a);
        b = find(b);

        // If parents are not equal, we union the two components.
        if (a != b) {
            if (sizez[a] < sizez[b]) {
                int temp = a;
                a = b;
                b = temp;
            }
            parent[b] = a;

            // Apply DSU by size: attach smaller tree to the larger one.
            sizez[a] += sizez[b];
        }
    }

    // Function to solve the problem.
    static int minCostToProvideWater(int n, List<Integer> wells, List<List<Integer>> pipes) {
        // Set to store the edges sorted on the basis of weights.
        TreeSet<List<Integer>> st = new TreeSet<>(new Comparator<List<Integer>>() {
            @Override
            public int compare(List<Integer> a, List<Integer> b) {
                return a.get(0).compareTo(b.get(0)); // Sort by cost
            }
        });

        // Inserting the edges into the set.
        for (List<Integer> e : pipes) {
            int u = e.get(0);
            int v = e.get(1);
            int wt = e.get(2);
            st.add(Arrays.asList(wt, u, v));
        }

        // Inserting the edges created by the pseudo vertex i.e. 0 (well-building).
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            st.add(Arrays.asList(wells.get(i), 0, i + 1));
        }

        // Initializing the DSU.
        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
            make(i);
        }

        int answer = 0;

        // Applying Kruskal's MST algorithm to find the minimum cost.
        while (!st.isEmpty()) {
            List<Integer> it = st.pollFirst();
            int wt = it.get(0);
            int u = it.get(1);
            int v = it.get(2);

            // If the villages are not yet connected, connect them and add the cost.
            if (find(u) != find(v)) {
                answer += wt;
                Union(u, v);
            }
        }

        return answer;
    }

    // Driver Function.
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int N = 3;
        List<Integer> wells = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2); // Cost of wells
        List<List<Integer>> pipes = Arrays.asList(
            Arrays.asList(1, 2, 1),
            Arrays.asList(2, 3, 1)
        ); // Cost of pipes between villages

        // Function call to calculate minimum cost to provide water.
        System.out.println(minCostToProvideWater(N, wells, pipes)); // Output the minimum cost.
    }
}

Explanation of the Code:

  1. Union-Find Setup:

    • We initialize a parent[] array to track the parent of each village, and a size[] array to maintain the size of each tree for optimization during union.
    • make(i) initializes each village as its own parent, and find(v) finds the root of a village.

  2. Kruskal's Algorithm:

    • We sort all edges by their weight (cost) using a TreeSet.
    • We add all edges, including the virtual edges representing the wells.
    • For each edge, if the two villages are not already connected (i.e., they belong to different sets), we add the edge's cost to the total cost and union the two villages.

  3. Final Output:

    • The final minimum cost is returned, which represents the minimum cost to either build wells or connect villages via pipes to ensure that every village has access to water.

Time Complexity:

  • Sorting Edges: O(E log E), where E is the total number of edges (wells + pipes).
  • Union-Find Operations: O(α(N)), where α is the inverse Ackermann function, which is nearly constant for practical input sizes.

Overall, the time complexity is dominated by the sorting step, i.e., O(E log E).

Space Complexity:

  • The space complexity is O(N + E), where N is the number of villages and E is the number of edges (pipes and well connections).

Notes:

  • Use path compression and union by size/rank for efficient DSU operations.
  • Virtual node 0 effectively models well-building cost as edges from 0 to each village.
  • This approach unifies well-building and piping into a single MST problem.
